target_customer: Women trying to conceive who buy a consumer at-home hormone monitor and test strips
problem: Ovulation tests give a yes or no on LH only. Inito measures estrogen, LH, PdG and FSH on one strip read by a smartphone-linked device to personalize fertile windows.
business_model: Consumer hardware starter kit ($149 with 15 strips) plus recurring test strip sales

founders.name: Aayush Rai
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder on the YC page; funding articles seen only as search snippets call him CEO. No bio opened.

founders.name: Varun AV
founders.background_notes: Named on the YC page; some coverage spells the name Varun A Venkatesan. No bio opened.

competitors.name: Mira (Quanovate)
competitors.what: At-home urine hormone monitor, first product a single-hormone LH tracker
competitors.traction_then: Launched September 2018 per a database summary
competitors.funding_then: Series A of $4.6M reported 2018-09-06 by CB Insights

technical_complexity.rationale: Quantitative multi-hormone lateral flow assays with a reader and smartphone image analysis demand assay chemistry, optics and software. Hard for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Multi-hormone single-strip assay and accumulated cycle data are hard to copy, but Mira and other monitors offer similar measurements.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors including Mira and Proov built multi-hormone products, but no incumbent bought Inito per the sources found.

market_need_then: Women trying to conceive already bought LH ovulation tests and fertility monitors in 2019, and Clearblue's monitor was an established but costly product. Inito targeted that existing spend with multi-hormone readings.

identity.visual_style: Clean consumer health site with testimonials and clinician endorsements

branding.community_and_virality: Site claims 200,000 plus couples trust it; review blogs compare it with Mira and Proov. No merch or fan community seen.

brand_strength.rationale: A distinctive short invented name that appears in many competitor comparison pages and reviews, but no sourced evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Inito is active with about 100 people and has raised a Series A in 2023 and a $29M Series B in December 2025, reaching about $45M total equity per press. It earlier raised about $9M from YC, physicians and family offices. Its multi-hormone strip differentiated it from single-hormone tests, and US launch followed.
notes: The Series A is confirmed by several outlets. The Series B amount and lead are confirmed by Entrackr, DealStreetAsia, YourStory and others. The roughly $9M earlier raise is stated by the Outlook India article without a stage label, so it is recorded as other with no date. Founding year 2015 and Siemens employment were stated only in search summaries of press and are not used for founders. FDA status was not confirmed; one profile lists Class I registration, treated as unverified. The Mira funding figure is from CB Insights alone and other databases disagree.
